tip: Water seedlings in the early morning before the heat rises to reduce evaporation and encourage deep root growth.
Inspect plants for pests and disease during mid-morning when symptoms are easier to spot on leaves.
Harvest fruits and vegetables in the late afternoon when temperatures are cooler and produce is less stressed.
Rotate crops in each bed every 4 to 6 weeks to reduce soil-borne pests and improve nutrient balance.
Test soil moisture before irrigation; aim for slightly damp soil rather than saturated ground.
Apply mulch after planting to retain soil moisture, suppress weeds, and moderate soil temperature.
Check weather forecasts first thing in the morning so you can adjust watering and spraying schedules.
Prune damaged leaves and spent blooms to improve air circulation and reduce disease risk.
Keep tools clean and dry after use to prevent rust and the spread of pathogens between crops.
Plant cover crops after harvest to protect soil, add organic matter, and reduce erosion.
Monitor soil pH monthly and amend it as needed for your crop’s preferred range.
Use shade nets or row covers in the hottest part of the day to protect tender crops from sunburn.
Record market prices and demand each week to plan harvests for the best value.
Inspect irrigation lines daily for leaks or blockages to conserve water and maintain even distribution.
Store seeds in a cool, dry place and rotate your seed inventory to keep germination rates high.
